If automated taxis were a thing, would you trust an automatic car over a taxi driver? Why?
Yes because they wouldn't be allowed on the road if they didn't work properly.
I'd trust a bot to not screw me over by purposefully trying to take the longest route or something similar.

As a programmer, no way in hell. I think people overestimate how good self driving cars are, even Google's. It's one thing for the car to mostly drive itself with a human in the driver seat to help when needed. It is quite another to have a car with no driver that I can tell to go to any address anywhere without any human assistance.

It is very reassuring to hear the only programmer respond so negatively. But aren't there already a few autonomous cars/trucks on the road and doing just fine? I haven't yet heard of any of them getting into at-fault accidents, and that is something I could see getting a lot of publicity

They all have drivers. There are no cars on the road that you can just type in an address and they will go there by themselves with no humans inside. The autonomy of the vehicles varies by the make and model. They are really partially self driving to varying degrees. Making one that is 100% self driving, such as would be required for the taxi, would be extraordinarily difficult to program. You'd have to have written an AI for it capable of common sense on the fly decision making, something relatively easy for the human brain but really really hard for computers. There's just so many variables and situations that could be encountered.

For example, I'd be willing to bet that if I had a Google car right now that it couldn't get out of my parking garage on its own. I live in an apartment and park on the 4th floor of a parking garage. The spiral route down to get out is not known to google maps. The garage is crowded and there is not room at the turns for 2 cars to pass so if I see a car coming up the turn while I'm going down I have to know to stop, wait for them to go around the bend. Has Google programmed in all the logic to handle that? Probably not. And there's probably a lot of other situations drivers deal with every day that it can't handle.

Now I have no doubt that if I had a Google car and just helped it out by driving it out of the garage myself down to a good known street that it could take over from there and do over 90% of the trip on its own. But there there is a big difference in difficulty in making a car able to drive 90 or 95% of the time on its own and having a car trustworthy enough to drive 100% of the time on its own carrying people anywhere they want to go.

The only caveat I will say is that maybe it would be feasible if the pickups and destinations were limited to a small known area, like a downtown. I can see that before I could see me able to buy a car that I could just type any address into and lie down in the back completely confident that the car can handle any situation that arises as well as a human.

I feel like when these cars do come onto the road though,they will be in busier areas and to work like taxis. I'm not expecting the car to be able to navigate parking lots/garages-if it were able to drop me off out front of the complex I'd be perfectly happy. There's no way that the car will be able to handle 100% of situations but if the cars could drive everywhere that Google maps covered I'd be very satisfied
